title: Introduce granular egress profiles and DNS handoff orchestrator
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes:
- Add configurable egress profiles that map control-plane subnets to AZ-aware NAT/EIP pools and route preferences.
- Add a DNS handoff orchestrator that stages Route53 forwarding and private hosted zone delegation with safety checks.
- Installer flags to opt into orchestrated handoffs and rolling peering updates.
- No forced user migrations; changes are opt-in via installer config.
description:
Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in multi-AZ VPCs frequently asked for finer-grained control over control-plane egress and safer DNS handoffs during upgrades and cross-account peering. The current installer only supports flat egress allocation and a single-step DNS forwarding change which has led to transient outages during large upgrades.

What this PR does: Introduces two coordinated features: (1) egress profiles: a Terraform module and installer interface for defining AZ/subnet->egress-profile mappings (NAT gateway or EIP pool selectors, allowed outbound CIDRs, and preferred route priorities); (2) DNS handoff orchestrator: a small orchestration service (runs as a Helm chart in the control plane) that performs staged Route53/private-hosted-zone delegation and conditional forwarding with canary traffic checks and automatic rollback on validation failures. Both are opt-in and backward compatible.

Design notes: Egress profiles live in terraform/modules/egress_profile and expose variables for preferred_nat_type, eip_pool_id (optional), allowed_outbound_prefixes, and weight for route priority. The installer translates the high-level installer flags into module inputs and generates a plan that can be reviewed. The DNS orchestrator implements a declarative plan: snapshots current DNS records, applies staged forwarding changes for a subset of subnets (canary), runs a probe suite (mesh of HTTP/DNS health checks using the existing observability hooks), and only proceeds to full handoff on success. Failure triggers a revert step that restores previous records and routes and sets an escalation annotation on the install job.

Testing and validation: Added terratest coverage for egress allocation permutation (tests/integration/test_egress_profiles.go) and an integration test that spins up a 3-AZ VPC in the CI integration harness and verifies canary handoff boundaries. Simulated Route53 propagation delay cases and validated orchestrator detects cutover regressions and reverts state. Also added unit tests for the orchestrator state machine.

Operational considerations and rollout: New installer flags: --enable-egress-profiles, --egress-profile-config (path to YAML), --enable-dns-orchestrator, and --dns-orchestrator-canary-percent. Default remains backwards compatible (all flags off). When enabled, the installer runs a preflight that outputs the planned terraform changes and a handoff plan. The orchestrator exposes a /health and /handshake endpoint and emits structured events to the existing audit log sink; we added a dashboard tile to the Redwood Console for canary progress and an alert rule that fires if a handoff step fails three times.

Security and compliance: Tightened security groups for control-plane egress endpoints; introduced a minimal IAM role template for orchestrator actions (assume-role only for Route53 and STS operations). We validated KMS policy scoping for EIP pool secrets and ensured no plaintext secrets are stored.

Rollback story: The orchestrator's revert path restores previous route53 entries and re-applies previous subnet routing with deterministic sequencing to avoid split-brain. The installer also writes a reversible plan file to the customer S3 bucket (or local path) so operators can trigger a manual rollback if needed.

Related work: Builds on ENG-4201 (subnet affinity allocator) and supplements prior work on conditional DNS forwarding (OPS-198). Addresses SUP-7291 which reported a customer outage during a forced DNS cutover.

How to review: Focus on terraform/modules/egress_profile for resource-level signoffs, the orchestrator state machine (installer/orchestrator/handshake.py), and the helm chart values for secure defaults. The PR contains a runnable demo guide under docs/installer/egress-profiles.md.

review_thread:
Diego: Please ensure the eip_pool_id input has clear failure semantics if left empty in cross-account setups.
Aisha: Added validation and a terratest case to ensure plan fails with a clear message when eip_pool_id is required but missing.
Priya: The orchestrator looks good but we should limit IAM permissions; can you narrow down Route53 actions?
Aisha: Reduced permissions to hostedzone:ChangeResourceRecordSets and route53:ListHostedZones; added assume-role pattern for cross-account access.
Martin: Canary percent default seems high — set default to 10%.
Aisha: Updated defaults and added CLI flag --dns-orchestrator-canary-percent with guard rails.
Diego: Tests are green in my local run, requesting approve.
Priya: Approving with the note to monitor the canary alert for first week.
Martin: Approved.
ci_details: Unit: pass; Lint: pass; Terratest: initial run found flaky net_alloc test, retried and passed; Integration: pass; E2E canary simulation: pass; total CI time: ~42m; note: one flaky terratest rerun recorded (rerun count: 1)
reason_for_change: Make control-plane egress allocation and DNS transitions safe and observable for private deployments; reduce outage risk during upgrades.
notes_for_ops: Enable feature by setting --enable-egress-profiles and supplying a YAML mapping; the installer will produce a plan file at <artifact_bucket>/egress-plans/<timestamp>.json. To abort a DNS handoff in progress POST /handshake/abort to the orchestrator service. Monitor the new console tile and the alert rule 'dns-handoff-failure'.
